title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented HWS rituals spanning arrival, academic recognition and the transition from student to alum.

cards.title: Begin College With a Handshake
cards.subtitle: The traditional first stop of HWS Orientation
cards.notes: Start Orientation on the Quad, where new students traditionally greet the HWS president and Mary Herlihy Gearan before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A face-to-face presidential greeting formally begins the arrival experience.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS reported in 2024 that every student's first stop at Orientation is traditionally a handshake with President Mark D. Gearan and Mary Herlihy Gearan.
cards.access_notes: An Orientation arrival tradition for incoming HWS students; follow the current Orientation schedule and check-in instructions.

cards.title: Write the Class Year in Light
cards.subtitle: An Orientation photograph made with phone lights
cards.notes: Bring a charged phone to Bristol Lawn and follow the event crew’s placement cues as the incoming class assembles its illuminated year.
cards.short_summary: Incoming students turn individual phone lights into one class-year photograph.
cards.evidence_claim: The official HWS Orientation 2025 photo gallery documents students gathering for Illumination on Bristol Lawn.
cards.access_notes: Held as part of Orientation; incoming students should use the current program for timing and participation directions.

cards.title: Hear Every New Hobart Name
cards.subtitle: Hobart’s opening-day roll call
cards.notes: Listen for the serial reading of every new Hobart matriculant’s name during the ceremony traditionally held before fall classes begin.
cards.short_summary: The Hobart academic year opens by naming each new member of the college.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hobart Deans describe John Henry Hobart Day as an August opening ceremony marked by a serial reading of every new Hobart matriculant's name.
cards.access_notes: Generally held the evening before fall-semester classes; ceremony roles and attendance depend on the current Hobart program.

cards.title: Set the Academic Awards at Dinner
cards.subtitle: Hobart recognition in Benjamin Hale’s name
cards.notes: Watch the Hobart Deans’ calendar for this April gathering, where departmental awards recognize scholarship and social contribution.
cards.short_summary: A namesake dinner joins academic honors with Hobart institutional memory.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS identifies the Benjamin Hale Dinner as an April Hobart tradition honoring academic achievement and social contributions, including departmental awards.
cards.access_notes: A recognition dinner for Hobart students and invited participants; consult the Deans for current eligibility and invitations.

cards.title: Leave With a Paddle
cards.subtitle: The Hobart Alumni Association welcome
cards.notes: At graduation season, look for the lakeside procession and the replica paddle that marks a senior’s transition into Hobart alumni life.
cards.short_summary: Soon-to-be graduates receive a paddle as their alumni welcome becomes literal.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hobart Deans state that the annual Hobart Launch, initiated in 2004, welcomes soon-to-be graduates into the Alumni Association and gives each one a paddle.
cards.access_notes: An annual graduation-season event for soon-to-be Hobart graduates; ceremony access follows Alumni Relations guidance.

cards.title: Close With “Hip Hobart, Forever!”
cards.subtitle: The song that ends formal Hobart meetings
cards.notes: At a formal Hobart gathering, stay through the close to hear the alma mater and its enduring “Hip Hobart, forever!” refrain.
cards.short_summary: Formal Hobart proceedings finish with a school song rooted in the nineteenth century.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS says the Hobart alma mater closes every formal meeting of Hobart College and documents its Cook and Rose authorship.
cards.access_notes: Observed at formal Hobart College meetings; attendance is determined by the particular ceremony or event.

cards.title: Gather for William Smith’s Founder
cards.subtitle: An annual tribute to the college’s namesake
cards.notes: Follow the William Smith Deans’ event notices for the yearly gathering dedicated specifically to founder and nurseryman William Smith.
cards.short_summary: William Smith students annually pause to recognize the person whose name their college carries.
cards.evidence_claim: The William Smith Deans state that students come together each year on Founder’s Day to pay tribute to William Smith, founder of the College.
cards.access_notes: An annual William Smith tradition; consult the Deans’ current event information for venue and participant details.

cards.title: Move Up in Class Colors
cards.subtitle: A shared HWS procession and recognition ceremony
cards.notes: Join the designated procession in your class color, then watch each cohort symbolically advance while campus awards are announced.
cards.short_summary: Colored cohorts process together and ceremonially advance to the next class year.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS reported that Moving Up Day began in 1905 and, beginning in 2025, combined the Hobart and William Smith observances into one event with two processions and symbolic class advancement.
cards.access_notes: The combined format began in 2025; participants should confirm the current procession start and assigned class color.

cards.title: Touch the Tree on the Hill
cards.subtitle: A revived William Smith luck ritual
cards.notes: During the official procession, pause at the tree on the bend of William Smith Hill—the documented touch is the ritual, not a guarantee.
cards.short_summary: A tree worn smooth by earlier students became a revived link between William Smith generations.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS documents that William Smith students touch the Good Luck Tree on the bend of the Hill, a tradition revived by alumna Alta Essom Boyer ’36.
cards.source_title: William Smith Class of 2023 Celebrated During Senior Toast
cards.access_notes: The documented touch occurs within William Smith senior traditions; avoid damaging the tree and follow ceremony directions.

cards.title: Plant the Graduating Class Tree
cards.subtitle: A living marker of William Smith class bonds
cards.notes: Follow the senior procession down William Smith Hill, where the graduating class helps plant a tree honoring its shared connection.
cards.short_summary: Each graduating William Smith class leaves a growing campus marker behind.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS reported that the William Smith Class of 2023 proceeded down the Hill for the traditional tree planting, which commemorates the class bond and honors founder William Smith.
cards.source_title: William Smith Class of 2023 Celebrated During Senior Toast
cards.access_notes: A graduation-season William Smith class ceremony; planting participation is organized through the official senior event.
